topics.topic: DFI Retail Group exit of 50% Maxim's Caterers stake and full control of Starbucks operations in seven Asian markets
topics.known_state: Announced in an SGX filing on Sept 29, DFI Retail Group will give up its 50% stake in Maxim's Caterers to Hongkong Caterers for cash proceeds of about US$340 million (S$434 million), and will assume full control of the Starbucks licensed business across Singapore, Hong Kong, Macau, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos, which generated close to US$750 million revenue in 2025 at a 7% underlying operating margin. Completion is expected by end of Q1 2027; DFI plans to use proceeds for M&A and shareholder returns, raising its dividend payout ratio to 80% in 2027 from 70%, targeting a mid-term operating margin of 8-9% and US$10 million in first-year synergies. The deal follows DFI's 2025 sale of its Singapore food business (Cold Storage, CS Fresh, Giant, Jason's Deli) to Macrovalue for $125 million.

topics.topic: Frasers Property and Mitsubishi Estate 51:49 JV to redevelop Valley Point and Fraser Suites Singapore
topics.known_state: Frasers Property and Mitsubishi Estate formed a 51:49 JV to redevelop Valley Point and Fraser Suites Singapore on River Valley Road into a luxury 999-year mixed-use project with around 407 luxury homes and sky villas, a new 184-unit Fraser Suites serviced residence, and dining, retail and lifestyle offerings, slated for sale launch in 2027 and completion in 2031. The 13,439 sq m site has maximum allowable gross floor area of 54,309 sq m, zoned commercial and residential; both existing assets cease operations on March 31, 2027. The JV acquired the Kallang Close land plot in April for $610.75 million ($1,415 psf ppr), and Frasers restructured some $2.1 billion of hospitality assets including consolidating full ownership of Fraser Suites Singapore.

topics.topic: GKE Corp buyback of 30 Pioneer Road warehouse from ESR-REIT for $32 million
topics.known_state: GKE Corp bought back the warehouse at 30 Pioneer Road from ESR-REIT for $32 million, matching its carrying value on ESR-REIT's books; GKE originally sold it to then Viva Industrial Trust for $45 million in 2016 under a sale and leaseback and has continued operating it. The property has a gross floor area of 26,1134 sqm and remaining lease of 10.6 years; GKE says the acquisition reduces its rental obligation ahead of the end of its JTC lease. Post-sale, ESR-REIT's portfolio comprises 66 properties in Singapore, Japan and Australia plus investments in three Australian property funds.

topics.topic: Metasurface Technologies dual primary listing on SGX Catalist
topics.known_state: Metasurface Technologies, a Singapore-headquartered precision component engineering company already listed on Hong Kong's GEM board (stock code 8637), lodged a preliminary offer document for a dual primary listing on SGX Catalist, with UOB Kay Hian as sponsor, issue manager and placement agent. Semiconductor manufacturing equipment accounted for 95.3% of group revenue in 1H2026; the company reported an S$46.3 million order book at 30 June 2026, estimated 114.1% precision-welding utilisation at its Singapore factory, and a 58% headline decline in reported profit to S$3.7 million in 1H2026, distorted by a prior-period S$6.4 million remeasurement gain and S$916,000 of SGX-listing expenses. Placement share count and price are undetermined; based on the recent HK$3.50-HK$3.60 Hong Kong trading range, an indicative SGX placement price of roughly S$0.53-S$0.56 per share is suggested, implying a pre-placement market cap of about S$81.7 million at S$0.55.

topics.topic: DFI Retail Group 1H interim results and raised interim dividend
topics.known_state: DFI Retail Group reported 11% higher underlying profit of US$117 million, free cash flow of US$382.7 million and net debt of US$22 million, and raised its interim dividend by 77% to US$0.062 per share.

topics.topic: Hongkong Land 1H interim results and raised interim dividend
topics.known_state: Hongkong Land reported underlying profit of US$259.1 million, with free cash flow falling to US$153.2 million on higher renovation spending and net gearing at 11%, and raised its interim dividend by 33% to US$0.08 per share.

topics.topic: Jardine Matheson interim results, dividend and US$2.4 billion I-MED Radiology acquisition
topics.known_state: Jardine Matheson reported adjusted underlying profit up 9% to US$735 million, with free cash flow down 23% to US$1.5 billion, and declared an interim dividend of US$0.65 per share (up 8%), guiding to a full-year dividend of at least US$2.47. It is ahead of a US$2.4 billion I-MED Radiology Network acquisition and announced a new US$500 million buyback.

topics.topic: PC Partner interim dividend of SGD 0.10 per share
topics.known_state: PC Partner Group declared an interim dividend of SGD 0.10 per share, more than doubled, payable 9 October 2026. Net profit surged 117.9% to HK$545.5 million on widening gross margins, backed by HK$2.5 billion in free cash flow and net cash of around HK$1.6 billion.

topics.topic: Civmec FY2026 full-year dividend of A$0,060 per share
topics.known_state: Civmec maintained its full-year dividend of A$0,060 per share for FY2026, payable 23 October 2026. Revenue rose 11.4% to A$903.0 million and net profit grew 22.5% to A$52.1 million, while free cash flow turned negative at A$28.5 million.

topics.topic: Union Gas interim ordinary and maiden special dividends
topics.known_state: Union Gas Holdings declared an interim ordinary dividend of S$0,0048 per share plus a maiden special dividend of S$0,0032 per share, payable 29 October 2026. 1H2026 net profit jumped 175.8% to S$12.0 million, driven mainly by its liquid fuel division, with S$25 million in free cash flow.

topics.topic: New World Development record annual loss, 11 Skies termination and balance-sheet repair
topics.known_state: New World Development posted a record HK$28.1 billion (US$3.6 billion) fiscal-year loss, driven by an HK$18.3 billion writedown after early termination of its agreement with the Hong Kong Airport Authority to manage the 11 Skies retail and office complex. Under the termination, New World will pay HK$3 billion and hand over three office towers and an entertainment venue at 11 Skies in April, removing a lease obligation estimated by UBS at at least HK$1.8 billion per year from 2028 through 2066. Chief executive Echo Huang said the firm is focused on repairing its balance sheet by paring debt and selling assets, including talks to sell its 50% stake in the Hyatt Regency hotel in Kowloon and spinning off a Shanghai project via a mainland China commercial REIT that could yield 3.24 billion yuan in net proceeds. Largest shareholder Chow Tai Fook Enterprises indicated it is prepared to provide financial backing following the record loss.
